questions.questionText: Which stage comes immediately after the egg in the butterfly life cycle?
questions.explanation: A butterfly develops from egg to larva, then pupa, and finally adult.

curriculum.skill: Apply living things and life cycles
curriculum.objective: Describe life cycles, food relationships and how structures or behaviours support survival.

questions.questionText: Which organism is the producer in the food chain?
questions.explanation: Grass makes its own food using light energy, so it is the producer.

curriculum.skill: Apply living things and life cycles
curriculum.objective: Describe life cycles, food relationships and how structures or behaviours support survival.

questions.questionText: Why do many desert plants have thick stems?
questions.explanation: Thick, fleshy stems store water that the plant can use during dry periods.

curriculum.skill: Apply living things and life cycles
curriculum.objective: Describe life cycles, food relationships and how structures or behaviours support survival.

questions.questionText: A disease greatly reduces the number of insects in a habitat. Which population is most directly at risk first?
questions.explanation: Specialist insect-eating birds lose their main food source when insect numbers fall.

curriculum.skill: Apply living things and life cycles
curriculum.objective: Describe life cycles, food relationships and how structures or behaviours support survival.

questions.questionText: In a test, drinks in A, B and C cool by 18°C, 11°C and 4°C. Which container is the best insulator?
questions.explanation: Material C shows the smallest temperature drop, so it is the best thermal insulator.

curriculum.objective: Compare material properties and distinguish reversible changes, irreversible changes and changes of state.

questions.questionText: Which arrow shows evaporation?
questions.explanation: Arrow B moves from liquid water to water vapour, which is evaporation.

curriculum.objective: Compare material properties and distinguish reversible changes, irreversible changes and changes of state.

questions.questionText: Which change is reversible?
questions.explanation: Melted chocolate can cool and become solid again without forming a new substance.

curriculum.objective: Compare material properties and distinguish reversible changes, irreversible changes and changes of state.

questions.questionText: A mixture contains iron filings, sand and salt. What should be done first to separate it?
options: Filter out the dissolved salt immediately
Use a magnet to remove the iron
questions.correctAnswer: Use a magnet to remove the iron
questions.explanation: A magnet selectively removes the iron before water is used to separate salt from sand.

curriculum.objective: Compare material properties and distinguish reversible changes, irreversible changes and changes of state.

questions.questionText: What is the resultant force on the cart?
questions.explanation: The forces oppose each other, so 8 N right minus 4 N left gives 4 N to the right.

curriculum.objective: Explain simple effects of forces and use models to describe Earth, Moon and Sun patterns.

questions.questionText: Which movement causes day and night?
questions.explanation: As Earth rotates, different parts face toward and then away from the Sun.

curriculum.objective: Explain simple effects of forces and use models to describe Earth, Moon and Sun patterns.

questions.questionText: Which force pulls an unsupported object toward Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity attracts objects with mass toward Earth.

curriculum.objective: Explain simple effects of forces and use models to describe Earth, Moon and Sun patterns.

questions.questionText: Why does a parachute fall more slowly when it opens?
options: Its larger area increases air resistance
questions.correctAnswer: Its larger area increases air resistance
questions.explanation: The open parachute pushes against more air, increasing the upward drag force.

curriculum.objective: Explain simple effects of forces and use models to describe Earth, Moon and Sun patterns.

questions.questionText: Why is the lamp off in the diagram?
options: The switch leaves a gap in the circuit
The wires form a complete loop
The lamp is connected to a wire
questions.correctAnswer: The switch leaves a gap in the circuit
questions.explanation: Current cannot flow around the circuit because the open switch creates a gap.

curriculum.objective: Build and interpret simple circuits and explain basic behaviour of light and sound.

questions.questionText: Which object will produce the darkest shadow?
questions.explanation: An opaque object blocks the greatest amount of light and forms the darkest shadow.

curriculum.objective: Build and interpret simple circuits and explain basic behaviour of light and sound.

questions.questionText: How can a drum produce a louder sound?
options: Cover it with a thick cushion
questions.explanation: A harder strike produces larger vibrations, which create a louder sound.

curriculum.objective: Build and interpret simple circuits and explain basic behaviour of light and sound.

questions.questionText: Two identical lamps are added in series to one battery. Why are they dimmer than one lamp alone?
options: Series circuits have no complete path
The available energy is shared across more components
questions.correctAnswer: The available energy is shared across more components
questions.explanation: In a series circuit, adding lamps increases resistance and the energy transfer per lamp is reduced.

curriculum.objective: Build and interpret simple circuits and explain basic behaviour of light and sound.

questions.questionText: Which factor did the pupils deliberately change between the three seed dishes?
options: Number of seeds in each dish
questions.explanation: The distance from the lamp is deliberately changed between the otherwise matching dishes.

curriculum.objective: Plan fair tests, read tables and graphs, identify patterns and evaluate the reliability of conclusions.

questions.questionText: Which conclusion is best supported by the results table?
options: Sugar never dissolves in cold water
Sugar dissolves faster in warmer water
questions.correctAnswer: Sugar dissolves faster in warmer water
questions.explanation: The dissolving time becomes shorter as water temperature increases.

curriculum.objective: Plan fair tests, read tables and graphs, identify patterns and evaluate the reliability of conclusions.

questions.questionText: Why should a measurement be repeated?
options: To change the question after every trial
To guarantee the prediction is correct
To check variation and calculate a more reliable average
To remove the need for units
questions.correctAnswer: To check variation and calculate a more reliable average
questions.explanation: Repeated measurements reveal variation and allow an average less affected by random error.

curriculum.objective: Plan fair tests, read tables and graphs, identify patterns and evaluate the reliability of conclusions.

questions.questionText: A plant-growth test uses different plant species in every pot. Why is the test not fair?
options: Growth has no relationship to conditions
Plant species is an uncontrolled variable
questions.correctAnswer: Plant species is an uncontrolled variable
questions.explanation: Different species may grow at different rates, so species must be controlled when another factor is tested.

curriculum.objective: Plan fair tests, read tables and graphs, identify patterns and evaluate the reliability of conclusions.
